data.body: COORDINATOR STATE CHECK absorbed; four adjustments recorded. (1) RP-04 S3 talismanic-profitable-isopod CLOSED - independently verified - so S3 runs in natural T1->T2->T3 order and S3 T3 is NOT deferred. (2) RP-04 did not remove the mutation-through-query pattern: it is still live at apply_handlers.py:261 inside _observe_rich_reemit, and RP-04 added a docstring at ~250-256 asserting that binding_store.py 'sits at the module-size cap and cannot carry a narrower accessor... If that file is ever split along a call-graph seam, give it a single-entry accessor and use it here.' Verified verbatim in the worktree. RP-02 S2 T3 adds exactly that accessor, so the docstring becomes FALSE when S3 T3 lands; S3 T3 must update it in the SAME change. Per the skill this is a NON-BEHAVIORAL comment-accuracy fix - applied directly, no manufactured change-detector test. (3) Attestations independently confirmed: epic/S1/S1T1 certified; S2, S3 and all remaining tasks UNSIGNED. review-plan will be earned mid-run IN DEPENDENCY ORDER (S2's only after S1 closes, S3's only after S2 closes); no front-loading and no --force. (4) MODULE-SIZE headroom verified against the real gate in .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml: the cap comparison is awk '$1 > lim', i.e. STRICTLY greater, so 800 passes and 801 fails; a non-blocking near-cap warning band starts at 720. Current: binding_store.py 799 (passes, in the warning band; T2 is what brings it down), run_differs.py 739 -> only 61 lines of headroom, so S3 T2 keeps the classifier in binding_recovery.py and limits the run_differs edit to the invocation; reconcile_helpers.py 758 -> S1 T3 preserves the five-file publication seam there without adding to it; apply_handlers.py 553 fine. Every intermediate stack commit must satisfy the cap, not just the final state - the cap number and lint/format rules are shipped in every implementer brief. Also confirmed none of binding_repository.py / binding_lifecycle.py / binding_recovery.py / docs/adr/0099 existed at branch point, so RP-02 is a clean start.
